item.title: Afghan children face narrowing path to education, UN agencies report
item.description: More than half of Afghanistan’s children who should be in primary school remain outside formal learning and millions of girls can only dream of going to university.

item.title: ‘The world is not ready’: Climate adaptation cash falls far short as warming heads past 1.5°C
item.description: Although global warming is set to exceed 1.5°C, financing to help communities adapt to climate change falls far short of needs, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) said in a report published on Wednesday.

item.title: UN peacekeeping chief warns of ‘security vacuum’ as Blue Helmets leave Lebanon and Western Sahara
item.description: The UN’s peacekeeping chief warned on Wednesday that the withdrawal of “Blue Helmets” from Lebanon and Western Sahara risks leaving a dangerous security vacuum, while the Security Council remains divided over what, if anything, should replace them.

item.title: Gunfire damages tents at Rafah displacement site in Gaza, as aid teams prepare for winter storms
item.description: Gunfire hit and damaged multiple tents at a displacement site in Gaza’s northern Rafah region on Tuesday, reportedly causing injuries and forcing a humanitarian partner to leave the area, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has said.

item.title: Fuel price shock: Why developing economies are paying the most at the pump
item.description: When war shut the Strait of Hormuz in February, oil prices soared everywhere. But the pain at the pump has been far from equal, and the world’s developing economies are paying the heaviest price, according to a new report from UNCTAD, the UN trade and development agency.

item.title: Syria’s undocumented children ‘pay the price’ of war and a law that shuts out mothers
item.description: Many children born in Syria since the war began in 2011 have no legal identity because nationality passes only through fathers – many of whom are dead or missing – a member of the independent UN commission investigating rights violations in the country said on Wednesday.

item.title: 15 years of ‘almost no progress’ in getting young people moving: WHO
item.description: One in four adolescents worldwide reported not getting at least 60 minutes of physical activity on any day in the previous week, according to new global estimates released by the World Health Organization (WHO) on Wednesday.

item.title: Pacific Scientists Build a Regional Picture of a Changing Ocean
item.description: From Fiji and Samoa to the Solomon Islands, Kiribati and Papua New Guinea, Pacific scientists are connecting research, monitoring and expertise to better understand how changing ocean chemistry is affecting the region's marine environments.
